newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-CHANG BEATS WOODBRIDGE IN MEMPHIS FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-CHANG BEATS WOODBRIDGE IN MEMPHIS FINAL.

text.p: Top seed Michael Chang ended nine years of frustration at the St. Jude tennis tournament Sunday by beating Todd Woodbridge in the finals of the $825,000 ATP Tour event.
Chang, the world's fourth-ranked player, had reached the semifinals at Memphis four times since turning pro here as a 16-year-old in 1988, but had never reached the championship singles match.
He made the most of his first appearance, however, beating the eighth-seeded Australian 6-3 6-4.
Chang, who celebrated his 25th birthday on Saturday, pocketed $120,000 and earned enough computer points to jump into number three when the next rankings are issued on Monday.
The diminutive American pressured the Australian's serve throughout. Chang broke Woodbridge's serve four times, despite the Australian saving nine other break-points.

Chang improved to 11-2 lifetime against Woodbridge, who won last month's Australian Hardcourt event in Adelaide to trumpet his emergence as a singles player. Woodbridge and compatriot Mark Woodforde are the world's top doubles team.
Against Chang, Woodbridge, who had not lost a set in reaching the final, was hampered by a rash of unforced errors. Chang broke the Australian in the second game of the match and in the eighth game.

Chang wasted little time in the second set, breaking Woodbridge in the opening game when Woodbridge netted a backhand. Chang stunned Woodbridge in the third game with a powerful forehand that led to another break and a 3-0 lead.
Chang finished it with a booming ace and immediately turned to his family in the stands and flashed a thumbs up.
"It is such a thrill for me to win here," Chang said. "This is definitely one of my favourite tournaments to come to year after year."

Woodbridge, winner of eight Grand Slam doubles titles, had an easier trip to the finals than Chang. The Australian's march included victories over 13th seed Jonas Bjorkman, unseeded Jeff Tarango and unseeded Brazilian Gustavo Kuerten, who upset second seed Andre Agassi in the second round.
Chang had to fight through Patrick Rafter, 15th seed Kenneth Carlsen, seventh seed Richey Reneberg and two-time Memphis champion Todd Martin in the semifinals.
"It was a tough week of tennis for me," Chang said.

Chang said he expected to see more of Woodbridge in the finals of tour events in the coming years. Woodbridge, ranked 32nd, said he's looking to reach the top 20 by year's end and hopes to perform better in singles at Grand Slam events.
Despite losing in straight sets, Woodbridge said he felt he played a more competitive match than in the past. Still, Chang's speed and quickness were too much to overcome.

"Michael has the best set of wheels in tennis," Woodbridge said. "What makes him so dangerous are the first two to three steps and the takeoff. He can get to balls that at first he's not sure where they are going."
